answer: Each identity holds one licensed pearl-oyster farm concession in a named lagoon: the registry logs its rafts, oysters and harvest, one concession per identity, duplicates refused. Each year inspectors count oysters at the nadir tide and test the water, which must stay crystal clear. One fake costs a 1,500-unit lease, 1,000 units of stock and fees, and 1,095 days to the first harvest; 100 fakes cost 250,000 units, 100 concessions, 300 farm-years. Cheapest cheat is renting one for 900 units a season, but the lender surrenders its own anchor, and bought pearls fail the registry tag check.
